text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two new local groups emerged this week to vie for a stake in Lonrho Zimbabwe's mining interests which are being unbundled and eyed by the government. President Robert Mugabe might have to intervene to end confusion and identify which group will negotiate to buy out the conglomerate's shares.
- Lawyers have filed a civil lawsuit with the high court seeking damages of Z$1.3 million from former state president Canaan Banana, who a police inspector alleges sodomised and sexually abused him.

- The Supreme Court has overturned a high court ruling which allowed companies owed money by the government to set the debts off against what they owed the state. The court said it was a not right, but a choice by the state to decide on whether to take any of the available options to settle.
- Paprika, a cash crop attracting the attention of many commercial farmers, will for the first time be sold through an auction system this year.
- Thousands of University of Zimbabwe students protested peacefully against a government decision to introduce a fee for courses at state-funded universities.

- Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe joins regional leaders in Zambia on Thursday for a summit of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) to discuss progress on reducing trade tariffs and non-tariff barriers, as well as alleged corruption and mismanagement in Comesa's secretariat.
